newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German November unemployment.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German November unemployment.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' comments on German November unemployment data, which showed a rise of 50,000 to a seasonally-adjusted 4.1 million. The unadjusted unemployment rate rose to 10.3 percent from 10.1 percent.
JAMES STEWART, SE BANKEN IN LONDON
"It's really quite substantially more than expected. The basic message that we are seeing from the economy is mixed...It's really unclear in which direction the economy is headed.

"It's quite possible that fourth quarter (growth) will be weaker but as we move into next year, we would expect exports to pick up as the global economy gathers momentum. There is excessive dependence on exports, but that is not unusual for the German economy. We expect slightly below trend growth."

"The labour market is a lagging indicator for the economy, so I'm still convinced that the recovery is on track. I would say that overall we should not have a too pessimistic view on the German economy."

"I think that the German economy is not on the recovery track as the last quarter showed. I think that in the fourth quarter the economy will flatten a bit. We expect growth of only 0.5 percent quarter-on-quarter in the fourth quarter (vs 0.8 percent in Q3) and this will continue next year.
The production for October and now the unemployment rate for November...show that the recovery is only export driven, and will flatten out in the next quarter and next year."

On whether the Bundesbank should consider cutting interest rates following the data, STEWART said: "Data from the real economy is mixed, and that would tend to suggest that caution is the wisest counsel at the moment."

KLAWITTER: "They will certainly wait until the first quarter of next year before we are quite optimistic that they will cut. The discount rate is 2.5 percent, but the Bundesbank is not as expansionary as this figure might suggest."

SOBOTTA: "Although we have had mixed data this week I don't expect a further rate cut. I don't think that the Bundesbank will cut the discount and Lombard rates next year, I just see a small move in the repo rate. I think the Bundesbank will wait for the (U.S. Federal Reserve) to raise the Fed Funds rates at the beginning of next year, so there is no room for the Bundesbank to cut rates."
On the outlook for the mark exchange rate:
KLAWITTER: "The Bundesbank is certainly happy around these levels. It doesn't take French demands for a lower franc/mark exchange rate too seriously."
STEWART: "I think the dollar will move a little bit higher, but not much -- within the 1.55-1.57 range...The Bundesbank is reasonably happy with this kind of rate."

SOBOTTA: "I think this is a fair level. On the other hand, I think the dollar could rise again against the mark by one to two pfennigs because of expectations of stronger growth in America and expectations somewhere in the market of a rate hike by the Fed."
